title: lore check and sync spawn one quest task view per task; use one task list per run cached by the .quest tree hash
description: DEC-282 item 1, filed from ODOC-610 (opum-doc, 2026-11-18T23:03Z). VERBATIM: 'lore-cli, with quest-cli for any field gap: one quest task list --json per run, never a per-task view. Missing fields are added to list's JSON (or a multi-id view) by quest-cli. Cache per run keyed by the .quest tree hash. Proof: measured at about 2000 tasks before and after, plus a test that the quest spawn count is bounded regardless of task count.' CONTEXT from the report: lore check and sync spawn one quest task view <id> --json per task, about 9 at a time, confirmed at src/adapters/quest.ts:456; 83 s wall per check at 574 tasks; on 2026-11-12 four to five concurrent runs made about 45 quest processes, a load of about 128, and a fleet shutdown. FIELD GAP MEASURED HERE on quest 0.14.1, 786 tasks: the lore:tasks rollup needs only id, title, status and the task file, and task list --json already carries id, title, status and path (path covers the file), so the per-task views are pure waste on this path. Fields detail() reads that list does NOT carry: subtasks, reporter and revision (all three exit 2 as unknown fields); file is covered by path. references, modifiedFiles and finalSummary ARE populated by list, checked against records that actually hold values rather than a null from a record that has none. Ships in the next lore/quest pair (DEC-282 items 1-4 ship together).

acceptanceCriteria.text: One quest task list --json per check and per sync run on the rollup path; no per-task task view spawns (measured: zero on that path).
The list read is cached per run, keyed by the .quest tree hash, and a changed tree invalidates the cache.
Measured at about 2000 tasks before and after, recording spawn count and wall time.
A test asserts the quest spawn count is bounded regardless of task count (N tasks, constant spawns).
Any field gap is named with the quest-cli ticket that adds it; today the rollup needs no gap, and subtasks, reporter and revision are named as the fields list lacks if a consumer needs them.

implementationNotes:
Built 2026-11-19 on branch fix/LCLI-791-one-quest-list-per-run. Rollup path (check, sync) now reads ONE quest task list per run via a new optional TrackerAdapter.taskRollup, cached across runs at .lore/cache/quest/task-list.json under sha256(quest version + every file under .quest). Zero task views on that path; lore tasks, link and orphans still view per task (unchanged); a backend without taskRollup falls back to per-task views.
Evidence: test/lcli791-quest-rollup.test.ts (6 tests): control = per-task path costs N views; total spawns identical for 3, 30 and 300 tasks with 0 views and 1 list; gatherReconciliation rows identical; missing id gives the same not_found; second run over an unchanged tree makes 0 list calls, a changed tree re-reads; corrupt cache is a miss. Test commit predicted the pre-build state (import failure); mutant forcing the per-task fallback gives 5 red with the control green. Full bun test: 5423 pass, 3 fail, all LCLI-614 real-quest race tests (known local pair-lock artifact, CI is the judge). typecheck and biome clean.
MEASURED, real quest 0.14.1 on this repo at 794 tasks (NOT the 2000 AC3 names, and the replaced operations rather than lore end to end, because the local pair lock refuses a real lore run): 794 quest task view at 8 concurrent = 26.5 s wall and 794 spawns; one quest task list = 0.146 s and 1 spawn. AC3 therefore stays UNCHECKED pending a 2000-task measurement.
FIELD GAP: none for the rollup (id, title, status, path all in list). task list lacks subtasks, reporter and revision, which only viewTask/detail consumers (lore link, lore tasks) read; no quest-cli ticket needed today.
